title: GitHub AI assistant for issues, pull requests and releases
h1: a github bot that reads the work before you weigh in
description: Give a bot in Metal a GitHub repo to follow. Get issue triage, pull request context and release notes, with clear limits on what it can change.
answer: **walk into standup knowing why the pull request stalled.** connect github to a Metal bot for issue context, changed files and release outlines. choose claude, chatgpt or another ai. a read-only bot brings the findings here. add labels, assignments or comments later, once you want it to act on the queue as well as read it.

review.by: lead agent: read against seo/facts, automated gate, independent fact-check pass

og_line: issues and pull requests, with context.

app.name: GitHub
app.intro: **find the workaround before asking someone to debug it again.** search earlier reports, read the issue and see what reviewers already said. these actions give the bot the context for a useful answer.

highlight.use: look for earlier reports of the same error before calling a bug new
read the reproduction steps and the original report
find the workaround someone already left in the comments
see which files a proposed change touches
read reviewer feedback before summarising what is blocked
gather commit messages for a release briefing
apply a triage label after you have agreed the rules
post a requested follow-up through the sending approval setting

app.setup:
**start with the repo you need for tomorrow's standup.** open **connected apps**, connect github and give your review bot read-only access. sign in on github's page, then name the exact owner and repository.

the catalog lists what github can do. your bot can use only the actions you allow.

routines_intro: **get the duplicate report, stalled review or release outline before the meeting.** pick one repo and one question. these routines return findings here. read the first few results before allowing writes.

routines.name: spot a duplicate report
routines.message: when an issue opens in amberquay/widget, read it and search earlier reports for the same error. tell me possible duplicates and missing reproduction details here. say when the evidence is thin. never label, assign, close or comment.
routines.output: possible duplicates and missing details, with issue references

routines.name: find who a review needs next
routines.message: every tuesday at 10, read open pull requests and reviews in amberquay/widget. group them by waiting for author, waiting for reviewer and unclear. name the review behind each choice. if none need attention, say so. leave github unchanged.
routines.output: a review queue grouped by who needs to act

routines.name: prepare release reading
routines.message: every thursday at 3, read commits in amberquay/widget since monday. draft a release outline here with fixes and additions separate. flag changes whose effect on customers is unclear. if no commits match, say so. never create a release or tag.

asks:
**let the bot read the queue before you let it run the queue.** comments count as sends and ask for **allow** or **deny** by default. a daily amount permits some sends on its own.

careful with **Full access**: a bot there with no sending rule can send up to 25 a day without asking. give it **Ask every time**.

labels, assignments, closures, merges and submitted reviews are other app changes. they don't wait for a send card. keep review bots read only; for writes, put 'ask me before you change anything' in the routine.
cannot: **keep merge and label tools outside a reading job.** read only blocks merges, labels and assignments before they reach github.
**give overnight triage an awake host.** local work stops during sleep or when dusk closes; dusk cloud works with your machine off.
**use the diff summary to decide what needs testing.** these routines gather evidence; they do not run code or reproduce the bug.

sections.h: give every report a repo boundary
sections.md:
**paste the full repo name so the right queue gets attention.** your github account may reach several projects. name the exact one in each routine.

explain what the labels mean before allowing label changes. if a report lacks reproduction steps, ask for them before calling the bug diagnosed.

the [issue triage routine](/routines/github-issue-triage) turns that into a recurring report.

sections.h: let each source answer its own question
sections.md:
**keep priority where the team plans the work.** if that's [linear](/integrations/linear), use linear for priority and github for issue and code context. a code comment shouldn't quietly rewrite the release plan.

a [slack digest](/integrations/slack) can add discussion. have the bot name the source behind each suggestion.

when sources disagree, put both in the report so the team can settle it.

faq.q: can i connect claude to github without building my own bot?
faq.a: **yes, connect github and pick the bot’s ai.** those choices are separate. changing ai keeps that bot’s chats and memory.

faq.q: can it close issues without asking me?
faq.a: **write access can permit closure without a sending card.** stay read only for advice, or tell the routine to ask before any change.

faq.q: where does my issue triage bot run when my laptop is closed?
faq.a: **local triage stops during sleep or when dusk closes.** dusk cloud gives the routine an always-on machine.

steps: connect github to a review bot with read only
ask for one issue and its earlier discussion
open the source issue or review before making the report repeat

worked.intro: an invented review example, not a customer result.
worked.before: ruth sees a stalled pull request and assumes it needs another reviewer.
worked.after: the bot points to the latest review asking for a failing test to be fixed. ruth follows up with the author. github stays unchanged.

mistakes.mistake: treating a diff summary as a passing test
mistakes.fix: ask what the bot read and what actually ran.
keep the review job read only.

tip.text: before chasing the reviewer, find out whether the author still owes a fix.
